changes.before: 2026-06-09 (Seattle City Council unanimous final passage of Council Bill 121214 and companion Resolution 32204, under emergency designation); signed by Mayor Katie Wilson 2026-06-11; Ordinance No. 127447
changes.after: 2026-06-09 City Council passage of Council Bill 121214 (9-0), enacted as Ordinance 127447; mayoral approval and clerk attestation 2026-06-11. Section 12 makes effectiveness contingent on council passage by a three-fourths vote and mayoral approval.

changes.before: 365 days from the effective date (immediate, under emergency designation), automatically expiring thereafter unless renewed for one or more additional six-month periods in accordance with RCW 36.70A.390; a public hearing is required within 60 days of adoption.
changes.after: Original term: 365 days from effectiveness under Sections 4 and 12; automatic expiry unless extended under statute or terminated sooner by Council. Section 9 permits one or more six-month renewals; Section 5 requires a public hearing within 60 days of adoption. Later renewals, termination and current operative endpoint remain unverified.

changes.before: Seattle Ordinance No. 127447 (Council Bill 121214, amended), with companion Resolution 32204 (amended); adopted under the RCW 36.70A.390 interim-zoning-control procedure. Amends SMC 23.84A.008 to define "data center" as a facility used primarily for storing and processing digital data, with power capacity over 20 Megavolt-Amperes and requiring uninterruptible power, and imposes a moratorium on the filing, acceptance, processing, or approval of applications to establish or expand such uses.
changes.after: Seattle Ordinance 127447 (Council Bill 121214), Sections 2-3: citywide moratorium on filing, acceptance, processing or approval of applications to establish, expand or change use to data centers, as principal or accessory uses. Definition requires primary use for computer/network equipment and digital-data functions, capacity above 20 MVA and generally uninterruptible power supplies with associated infrastructure. Section 2 exempts expansions of no more than an additional 20 MVA at facilities operating on the effective date that meet the definition or would meet it except for existing capacity at or below 20 MVA. Section 6 adopts Attachment A work plan under RCW 36.70A.390.

changes.before: Five proposed large-scale data centers reportedly seeking Seattle City Light service, with combined maximum demand of 369 MW (about a third of Seattle's average daily power consumption); public concern over ratepayer, environmental justice, and power-supply impacts
changes.after: Ordinance findings identify company interest in large-scale data centers and potential cumulative impacts on energy and water infrastructure, utility affordability/reliability, public health, environment and economic development. Project counts and aggregate MW demand are not established by this ordinance review.

changes.before: Active. Adopted by City Council 2026-06-09 (unanimous), signed by Mayor Wilson 2026-06-11. Companion Resolution 32204 directs a study/policy process (grid capacity, water use, utility rates, land use, jobs, and public health impacts) with reports and proposed permanent legislation due by January 2027. Two data center projects that were already vested under prior rules are not covered by the moratorium; new applications from companies including Prologis, Equinix, and Sabey are paused pending the study process. No source dated after early-to-mid summer 2026 was located to further update this status as of 2026-07-31.
changes.after: Original adoption confirmed: Council passage 2026-06-09 (9-0), mayoral approval and clerk attestation 2026-06-11. Sections 11-12 declare immediate effectiveness upon qualifying council passage and mayoral approval. The legacy active classification is retained, but later amendments, extensions, early termination, litigation and current enforceability remain unverified. Original work-plan deadlines do not establish completion; project-specific vesting or applicability is not determined by this review.

changes.before: Five proposed Seattle data centers, 369 MW combined maximum demand, per Seattle Times report (2026-04-10) and GeekWire follow-up (2026-04-19)
changes.after: No project-specific applicability or aggregate demand is accepted from this review. The earlier inventory reported five proposals totaling 369 MW and named developers; those assertions remain historical, unverified project leads rather than established applications covered by Ordinance 127447.

changes.before: Moratorium enacted 2026-06-09; the city is using the pause and the companion Resolution 32204 working-group process to study grid, water, ratepayer, and environmental-justice impacts and to develop permanent siting/zoning rules, with reports and proposed permanent legislation due by January 2027.
changes.after: Ordinance 127447 adopts the moratorium and Attachment A work plan. Original deadlines: City Light electricity analysis/proposal July 1, 2026; Public Utilities water analysis/proposal October 30, 2026; construction/inspection zoning analysis and proposed legislation January 2027, with anticipated Council action March 2027; sustainability-led community-benefits framework February 1, 2027. Delivery, subsequent legislation and current legal force remain unverified. Companion Resolution 32204 is a separate instrument whose terms are not established by these sources.
